newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Tax woes hit Paris as European stocks flag.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tax woes hit Paris as European stocks flag.

text.p: European share markets were mostly weaker on Friday, with Paris the chief casualty as investors fretted over possible company tax hikes to fix the French budget for European monetary union.

London went against the trend of profit-taking on leading continental bourses. But the buying, dictated largely by technical factors, faded acoss the morning and the market again failed by a whisker to break 5,000 points.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar firmed against the mark following comments from Chancellor Helmut Kohl suggesting that Germany was not too worried by the mark's drop.
Political worries were the main problem for the Paris bourse, with investors jittery before the new Socialist-led government releases an audit of public finances on Monday.

A government source said ministers were studying a possible increase in corporate tax and raising company social security contributions to cut the budget deficit, which is expected to be around 3.6 percent of gross domestic product -- well above the 3.0 percent target for joining the single European currency.

That news pushed the CAC-40 index of blue chips down 54.04 points or 1.83 percent at 2,904.55 by midday. However, investors were also cautious, awaiting the release of May U.S. trade figures at 1230 GMT for any effect on the dollar.

Shares in Club Mditerrane went against the trend, jumping on news that the Trigano family, which founded the leisure empire, had quit the supervisory board. They were up 3.81 percent even though the company, now run by the former boss of the Euro Disney theme park, reported a 413 million franc ($68.2 million) first-half loss.
German shares, which closed at a record high on Thursday, suffered from profit-taking. The DAX index of blue chips was down 37.30 points or 0.88 percent at 4,190.01.

"I think the market looks a bit tired," said one Frankfurt dealer. "We could fall rather quickly today like we did on Thursday for no apparent reason. The market needs to take a rest before moving higher."

Dealers blamed some of the losses on the expiry of the DAX options due to signs of heavy open interest at 4,200 points. Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial average closed down 18.11 points at 8,020.77 overnight, also weighed on sentiment.
London went against the trend, with the FTSE-100 index climbing to less than two points below the 5,000 level.

But, not for the first time this week, the market failed to break the pyschological barrier and by late morning it had lost most of its gains. The FTSE was up 10.7 points at 4,959.7, down from a record intradday high of 4,998.1.

Dealers said the FTSE had been dragged up by the expiry of July options, rather than any renewal of the feverish buying seen earlier in the week. "There are not many reasons to chase the market higher this morning, there are more to want to stay out," one dealer said.

On the foreign exchanges the dollar gained against the mark after Helmut Kohl said a somewhat stronger dollar was not an earth-shaking matter. This seemed to confirm market suspicions that Germany is not too worried about the mark's recent steep fall against the dollar and other European currencies, which in case has helped the country's exporters.

"When exports used to go badly because of a weak dollar, people complained," Kohl told a news conference. "Now things are going a bit the other way, which is not earth-shaking. It does not mean that we should start moaning again."
The dollar was at 1.7980 marks, down from 1.7998 at the European close on Thursday but up from earlier on Friday.

It was also at 115.73 yen, down from 116.07 on Thursday. This followed the annual report from the Japanese Economic Planning Agency (EPA), which said the country's economic recovery was close to self-sustaining.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar was at 115.73 yen and 1.7980 marks compared with 116.07 yen and 1.7998 marks in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 10.7 points at 4,959.7, down from a record intradday high of 4,998.1.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index of floor trade was down 37.30 points or 0.88 percent at 4,190.01.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 54.04 points or 1.83 percent at 2,904.55.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the morning at $323.45 an ounce compared with Thursday's morning fix of $319.40. Silver was eight cents higher at $4.27. ($ = 6.056 French Francs)
